claim.quote: Three independent analyses have been performed and no evidence for neutrino oscillations has been found. The resulting limits onAm 2 for maximal mixing are more restrictive by more than one order of magnitude with respect to earlier measurements.

date.locator: journal page header (issue date; received 19 April 1990)
date.note: Issue date printed on the page header of Phys. Lett. B 245, 305-310.

name: A study of atmospheric neutrino oscillations in the Fréjus experiment

summary.plain: Fréjus counted atmospheric-neutrino interactions in its iron detector and compared electron-type with muon-type events. It found no sign of neutrino oscillations, and set limits on the mass-squared difference tighter by more than ten times than earlier ones.
summary.technical: 1.56 kt yr of fiducial sensitivity; electron-to-muon charged-current ratio compared with a Monte Carlo including nu_mu-nu_e, nu_e-nu_tau and nu_mu-nu_tau oscillations; three independent analyses find no evidence for oscillations.

title: A study of atmospheric neutrino oscillations in the Fréjus experiment
why_it_matters: An early underground limit on atmospheric-neutrino oscillations, set well before the Super-Kamiokande oscillation evidence of 1998.
